title: SMB Data Processing Agreement + Security Rider (draft)
body:
Purpose
This Data Processing Agreement ("DPA") with attached Security Rider is a simplified, SMB-friendly template intended for small and mid-market customers integrating Redwood Inference hosted API endpoints. It balances legal coverage with short execution time and reduces negotiation cycles for low-risk, low-volume integrations.

Parties
This DPA is entered into between: (1) Redwood Inference, Inc. ("Processor") and (2) [CUSTOMER NAME] ("Controller"), effective as of [EFFECTIVE_DATE].

1. Definitions
- "Personal Data": personal data as defined under applicable Data Protection Law.
- "Processing": any operation performed on Personal Data.
- "Subprocessor": any third party engaged by Processor to Process Personal Data on behalf of Controller.
- "Data Protection Law": applicable laws governing processing of Personal Data (e.g., GDPR where applicable).

2. Scope and Roles
- Controller instructs Processor to Process the categories of Personal Data and Data Subjects described in Section 3 for the purposes set out in the Master Services Agreement ("MSA") or applicable ordering document.
- Processor will only Process Personal Data as necessary to provide the services and as documented in this DPA.

3. Data Processing Details (summary)
- Categories of Data Subjects: end users of Controller’s service, Controller employees, and support contacts.
- Categories of Personal Data: identifiers (name, email), account metadata, and query text where it contains personal data.
- Nature of Processing: collection, transmission, storage, ephemeral inference, logging for debugging and billing.
- Duration: duration of the MSA plus a 90-day transitional retention period unless otherwise requested.
- Location: primary processing in Redwood hosted regions specified in the order; backups may be stored in [REGION_LIST].

4. Security Rider (summary; non-exhaustive)
Processor commits to maintain the following baseline controls for SMB customers: 
- Encryption: TLS 1.2+ in transit; at-rest encryption using AES-256 for persistent storage.
- Access controls: role-based access, MFA for admin accounts, least-privilege for service accounts.
- Network protections: VPC peering or private link options for eligible plans, IP allow-listing for API keys.
- Logging & monitoring: retention of critical logs for 90 days; alerting for infrastructure-level incidents.
- Patch management: critical security patches deployed within 14 days; high-risk within 7 days where feasible.
Note: For enterprise/private deployments, reference the full Security Annex. This rider is intentionally concise for SMB transactions.

5. Subprocessors
- Controller authorizes Processor to engage subprocessors listed at https://www.redwood.com/subprocessors (live list). Processor will: (a) provide notice of new subprocessors via the dashboard or email; (b) enter written contracts with subprocessors with data protection obligations at least as protective as this DPA.
- Right to object: Controller may object to new subprocessors on reasonable grounds (data residency, compliance concerns) within 10 business days of notice. If objection cannot be resolved, either party may terminate the applicable Order.

6. Incident Response and Notification
- Processor will notify Controller without undue delay and no later than 48 hours after becoming aware of a security incident materially affecting Controller’s Personal Data. Notification will include: summary of impact, root cause (if known), immediate mitigations, and planned remediation steps.
- For SMB plans, initial notification will be high-level; detailed forensic reports provided under reasonable commercial terms.

7. Data Subject Rights
- Processor will assist Controller, to the extent reasonably possible, with requests to exercise data subject rights under applicable Data Protection Law (access, rectification, erasure, portability, restriction). Assistance is scoped to available tooling and logs maintained by Processor.

8. Retention and Deletion
- Upon termination or expiry of the MSA, Processor will delete Controller Personal Data from production systems within 90 days and purge backups within 180 days unless retention is required by law.
- Controller may request earlier deletion for specific assets and inclusive of a verification certificate where feasible.

9. Audits and Evidence
- For SMB customers, Processor provides: (a) standard SOC2 Type II summary report on request (redacted), (b) compliance FAQ and evidence pack using pre-prepared artifacts.
- Onsite audits and extended pen-testing evidence are available for enterprise via paid review.

10. Liability and Limitation
- Processor liability for breaches of data protection obligations is subject to the liability clauses in the MSA. For SMB Orders, the maximum aggregate liability for Processor for Data Protection claims is limited to the higher of $250,000 or 6 months of fees paid under the Order.

11. Termination
- Material breach of this DPA gives the non-breaching party the right to terminate the applicable Order if breach is not cured within 30 days of written notice.

12. International Transfers
- Processor may transfer Personal Data across borders using standard contractual mechanisms or other lawful transfer tools; Controller may specify residency constraints in the Order (subject to plan availability).

13. Governing Law and Miscellaneous
- Governing law: [GOVERNING_JURISDICTION] as set in the MSA.
- This DPA is incorporated into the MSA between the parties. Where inconsistency exists, the DPA prevails for Data Protection obligations.

SIGNATURES
[REDWOOD SIGNATURE BLOCK]
[CONTROLLER SIGNATURE BLOCK]

---
INTERNAL NOTES AND NEGOTIATION GUIDANCE (for Security & Legal teams)
- Purpose: reduce friction for small customers who require a DPA but do not need extensive enterprise annexes. Use when Order TCV < $100k/year and data residency needs are standard.
- Negotiation playbook:
  * Accept reasonable requests to shorten log retention by 30–60 days but flag impacts to debugging/billing.
  * For objections to subprocessors, attempt technical mitigations (IP allow-list, region pinning) before escalating to Legal.
  * If customer requests detailed forensic reports, offer a paid incident analysis engagement.

Quick checklist before sending to customer:
- Update [REGION_LIST] with the customer’s requested region(s).
- Attach SOC2 summary and relevant question matrix.
- Confirm retention/backup window aligns with order and note any deviations.
- Populate [GOVERNING_JURISDICTION] and [EFFECTIVE_DATE].

TODOs (draft stage)

- Security: confirm patch SLA language and whether to offer 30/14/7 tiered commitments.
- Sales/AE: collect customer residency preference and provide to Legal before execution.

Revision history
- 2024-11-05: initial draft by Asha Patel.
- 2024-11-12: added Security Rider baseline controls (Marco Ruiz).

End of document.
